title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is studying solutions of the 'équation des lacets' for the profinite fundamental group π̂_{0,3}, the free profinite group on two generators of P^1 minus {0,1,∞}. These are pairs (multiplier, ξ) of the kind that make up the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group GT-hat: ρ = 2σ+1 ∈ Ẑ* plays the role of the cyclotomic λ, and ξ the role of f. Here the relations are pushed down to the quotient SL(2,Ẑ)' (SL(2,Ẑ) modulo ±1) through Γ(2) → SL(2,Ẑ).

On the previous page the 2-cycle relation (**) becomes, in the quotient, B + 2σD = C, i.e. C − B = 2σD. Using C − B = 1 − D this is ρD = 1 (93). The sign ambiguity (h_0 = ±ᵗh_0) is excluded because ξ ≡ 1 mod 2.

The 3-cycle relation (64) is solved parametrically as ξ = λρ(λ)^{-1}, where ρ is the order-3 rotation and λ ∈ GL(2,Ẑ) with det λ = δ = ±1.

On this page:
- Formula (78) gives A, B, C, D as quadratic forms in the entries a, b, c, d of λ. In particular D = δ(c² + cd + d²), with the convention δ = −1 in case 2'.
- (93) becomes (96): (2σ+1)D = 1, i.e. pD = 1.
- So the multiplier is read off from the image of ξ in SL(2,Ẑ)' by (97): p = 1/D.
- The ±1 ambiguity of D in SL(2,Ẑ)' is removed by the choice of λ; λρ(λ)^{-1} does not depend on the sign of λ.

Arithmetic consequence: c² + cd + d² is the norm form of the Eisenstein integers Z[ζ_3]. Mod 3 it takes only the values 0 and 1. D must be a unit, so the value 0 is excluded. Hence D ≡ δ mod 3, so p ≡ δ mod 3.

The next page turns this into a dichotomy:
- p ≡ 1 (3), i.e. σ ≡ 0 (3), exactly when ξ = λρ(λ)^{-1} with λ ∈ SL(2,Ẑ);
- p ≡ −1 (3) exactly in the twisted case ξ = λ' l_0^{-1} ρ(λ')^{-1}, where D = 3c² + 3cd + d² (another form of discriminant −3) and pD = −1.

In short, the page computes how the multiplier of a solution is detected in the SL_2 quotient, and relates the cyclotomic character mod 3 to which branch of the 3-cycle parametrization one is in.
errors: No real error. The mod-3 case check is correct: c=0 or d=0 gives a square (0 or 1); c,d=±1 gives 1+1±1 ≡ 0 or 1.

p ≡ ±1 mod 3 holds trivially for any unit of Ẑ. The real content is the correlation between the sign and the branch (δ = det λ), and this depends on the parametrization (70) covering all solutions, which is not re-proved here.
Minor: C − B = 1 − D is used silently. It is derived from AD − BC = 1 together with the relations from (78).

ideas.what: Projecting the 2-cycle relation f(x,y)f(y,x)=1 to SL(2,Ẑ)/±1 gives the linear relation (2σ+1)D = 1, so the multiplier is the inverse of the lower-right entry of the image of ξ
ideas.modern_name: Image of GT-hat elements under F̂_2 ≅ Γ̂(2) → SL_2(Ẑ); modular/congruence quotient of GT
ideas.usually_credited_to: Related work by Ihara, Lochak–Schneps, Nakamura on GT and its SL_2 quotients (1990s)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme only sketches GT-type ideas; this computation is not published

ideas.what: Parametrizing solutions of the 3-cycle relation as ξ = λρ(λ)^{-1} gives D as the Eisenstein norm form c²+cd+d²
ideas.modern_name: Norm form of Z[ζ_3]; Lang/Hilbert-90-type parametrization of solutions of xρ(x)ρ²(x)=1

ideas.what: Mod-3 argument: the branch of the parametrization (det λ = ±1, or the twisted l_0 case) is determined by the multiplier mod 3
ideas.modern_name: Cyclotomic character mod 3 versus a norm from Z_3[ζ_3]* (local norm-index-2 phenomenon at 3)

missed.claim: Through the SL_2 quotient, the multiplier of a solution of the lacets equations is the inverse of a norm from the Eisenstein integers. Its residue mod 3 decides which branch of the 3-cycle parametrization the solution lies in. This is a local class-field-type obstruction at 3 for the GT-type relations in the modular quotient.
missed.quote: la forme quadratique c^2+d^2+cd ... ne prend que les valeurs 0 et 1 ... Or ici on doit trouver une unité, la valeur 0 exclue
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a small explicit invariant separating classes of solutions of the 3-cycle relation in GT-hat-like groups. It may relate to known work on the image of GT-hat in SL_2(Ẑ) and to Ihara's results, but I have not seen it stated in this form.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a concrete, unpublished computation of GT-type relations in the SL_2 quotient with a neat mod-3 Eisenstein-norm argument. It is mostly elementary, and similar quotient computations exist in the 1990s GT literature.
transcription_corrections: 'la multiplication p' should be 'le multiplicateur p'.
'λ g(λ)^{-1}' should be 'λ ρ(λ)^{-1}': ρ is the rotation, not g.
'dans la valeur 0 exclue' should read 'une unité, la valeur 0 exclue, donc'.
